title: Python Compatibility and Canonical Rust-Core Cutover

preflight.note: Created before Python/Rust authority cutover, compatibility binding/protocol, or native distribution migration begins; activation is gated on prior Rust parity work.

acceptance_criteria.text: Record a durable cutover decision identifying canonical Rust-supported surfaces, remaining/deferred surfaces, required parity evidence, Python compatibility mechanism, versioning, packaging, rollback, release implications, WI050 boundary status, and permitted documentation claims.

Evaluate PyO3/native binding and a stable Rust executable/protocol against actual Windows/Linux/macOS packaging, Python-version, API/diagnostic, development, offline/source-build, performance, and release-maintenance evidence before selecting the compatibility architecture.

The selected end state has one explicit canonical executable authority for each migrated semantic surface; Python and Rust are not left as indefinitely independent canonical validators/mutators for the same supported behavior.

Require durable read/discovery, validation/diagnostic, mutation before/after, generated-projection, transactional recovery, compatibility-interface, platform packaging, and known-non-parity evidence before flipping canonical authority.

For migrated commands, preserve practical Python CLI/user compatibility by making Python a tested client/wrapper of Rust authority rather than retaining a silent independent implementation; intentionally retained Python-only surfaces are labeled explicitly.

Define and test compatibility/version negotiation and structured error/diagnostic transport across the selected Python/Rust boundary, including mismatched versions and missing/incompatible Rust runtime behavior.

Provide reproducible Windows/Linux/macOS distribution for the selected architecture with documented artifact/version coupling, checksums/provenance, install/update behavior, offline/source-build story, and rollback/recovery to the available execution level.
Do not modify frozen CI/release paths without the existing separate operator-approval process; a cutover plan may identify such required changes but does not bypass frozen-surface governance.

WI050 admission/enforcement does not migrate automatically with canonical-core cutover; if no separately proven Rust protected substrate exists, those security-critical operations remain explicitly on their existing authority path.

Documentation and release notes distinguish canonical Rust-supported semantics, Python wrapper/client status, intentionally deferred surfaces, platform/package limitations, WI050 enforcement status, and compatibility guarantees without overstating migration completeness.
Provide an explicit rollback plan that does not require rewriting repository history or silently downgrading durable governed record formats when a compatibility/package release fails.

Closeout evidence demonstrates the selected compatibility architecture, canonical-authority transition, supported platform distribution, regression/conformance results, rollback path, exact deferred/non-parity list, and consistency between implementation evidence and public claims.
